title: GPU SKU liquidity and staggered order playbook
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures an operational playbook for maximizing fleet liquidity (ability to reallocate, resell, or repurpose arriving GPUs) while smoothing arrivals via staggered orders to match onboarding windows and reduce peak staging cost. Goal: reduce burst capacity cost and mitigate long-lead-time supplier variance without increasing out-of-capacity incidents.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to all accelerator SKUs used for inference pools (A100 variants, H100 variants, and Q-compressed ASICs).
- Planning horizon: 12 weeks rolling, with tranche decisions every 2 weeks.
- Supplier lead times are stochastic; use p50/p75/p90 bands. We assume base p50=6 wks, p75=9 wks, p90=13 wks for offshore shipments.
- Redistribution (cross-region transfers) cost estimated as 1–2% of unit list plus shipping; dry-run reimaging time 4–8 hours.

Key operational levers:
1) Staggered tranches: split large orders into 3 tranches (early, mid, late) to align with capacity onboarding and expected attrition.
2) Liquidity lanes: classify SKUs by liquidity tier (High, Medium, Low) for prioritizing transfers and trade-ins.
3) Safety buffer buckets: maintain regional buffers in two forms — hot (immediately deployable) and warm (requires reimage).
4) Contingency lanes: pre-approved suppliers/spot-lanes for 1–2 wk emergency purchases at premium.

Decision matrix (high-level):
- If regional utilization > 78% and 2-week forecast net add > 10% of region hot capacity => escalate to procurement to advance early tranche by 1–2 weeks.
- If lead-time variance (p90-p50) > 5 weeks => shift to more tranches and increase warm buffer by +15%.
- If >3% of units idle in region for >14 days => flag for transfer liquidation or temporary resell program.

12-week rolling forecast (example snapshot):
Week,Projected token-qps growth %,Net add GPUs needed (hot),Planned arrivals (tranche)
W1, +2, +8, 0
W2, +4, +12, Tranche A: 10 units (arriving W4-W5)
W3, +3, +9, 0
W4, +5, +15, Tranche B: 12 units (arriving W7-W8)
W5, +1, +3, 0
W6, +6, +18, Tranche C: 18 units (arriving W10-W12)

Lead-time bands and recommended actions:
- p50 (6 wks): plan normal tranche cadence.
- p75 (9 wks): move to 3-tranche split if single order >30 units.
- p90 (13 wks): open contingency lanes and prioritize higher-liquidity SKUs for transfer.

SKU liquidity classification (example):
- High liquidity: H100 SXM-80GB (strong aftermarket, easy to reallocate)
- Medium liquidity: A100 PCIe-40GB (common, moderate demand)
- Low liquidity: Early gen 80GB with proprietary coolers (niche resale, keep as warm buffer only)

Cross-region transfer policy (quick rules):
- >72h approval: transfers that require policy exception (e.g., compliance checks).
- <72h approval: standard transfer within same legal region if hot capacity shortfall >10%.
- Transfer cost cap: $X per unit (finance-updated). If transfer cost > cap, prefer expedited procurement or temporary burst in-hosted region.

Sample tranche recommendation template (to send to procurement):
- SKU: H100-80GB-SXM
- Total units requested: 40
- Recommended split: A=10 (accelerate onboarding), B=12, C=18
- Lead-time expected: p50=6, p90=13 (notes: vendor batch constraint weeks 7–9)
- Rationale: match onboarding windows (weekly ramp) and reduce staging peak in US-WEST
- Contingency: pre-approve 6 units via spot-lane if actual arrivals slip beyond p75.

Liquidity operations playbook (day-to-day):
- Weekly cadence: procurement sync (Wed), SRE capacity review (Thu), Transfer triage (Ad-hoc).
- Fast-path actions (within 24h): allocate warm buffer to hot pool by reimage if shortfall <8 GPUs and time to scale <12h.
- Slow-path actions (24–72h): initiate cross-region transfer and update route table for traffic weight shift.
- Emergency (>72h): engage spot-lane vendors and enable degraded routing to smaller models to preserve latency SLOs.

Metrics to track (dashboard suggestions):
- Regional hot utilization % (by region and model family)
- Days to redeploy warm buffer -> hot (median, p90)
- Tranche slippage (planned arrival delta weeks)
- Transfer acceptance rate and cost per unit
- Idle unit-days >14 (liquidation trigger)

Example scenarios and recommended responses:
1) Supplier outage pushes p75 to 16wks mid cadence:
   - Immediate: pause late tranche shipments, increase warm buffer allocation by 20%, kick contingency-lane procurement for high-liquidity SKUs.
   - Medium-term: revisit trimestral SKU mix to favor high-liquid SKUs for next 3 orders.
2) Unexpected demand spike in APAC (+18% token growth over 3 weeks):
   - Immediate: reweight routing to reduce APAC-bound batch sizes by 10% and move 6 warm units from EU to APAC via expedited transfer.
   - Follow-up: accelerate next tranche for APAC by 1 week if projected shortfall persists.

Open questions / next actions:
- Confirm finance transfer cost cap and update transfer cost per unit placeholder ($X).
- Validate spot-lane vendor list and emergency purchase cadence (legal + procurement).
- Run simulation this quarter using observed lead-time distribution from vendor telemetry (JIRA-INF-1172).

Notes to operators (quick):
- When recording tranche dates in procurement sheet, always tag with vendor batch id and port ETA (not just ship date).
- Keep at least one SKU family in warm buffer across all regions to allow quick cross-region remapping.
- This playbook should be reviewed after any tranche slip >2 weeks or any cross-region transfer >50 units.
